C1_closed_loop.scenario: policies/urban_demo_policy.yaml; instruction 'fly to (40, 40) at 6 m/s altitude 20'; spawn (0, 0); the policy's no-fly zone lies on the straight line

C1_closed_loop.assist: none: goal blend 0, no planner, no path follower. Assisted runs are recorded as assisted and are not C1.
nulls: stub P-controller, given the target coordinates: the no-learning reference a learned backend has to beat
C1_closed_loop.status: not flown on hil by any backend; each row of the table states why (BACKENDS[<backend>]['c1'])

C2_follow_closed_loop.added_after_the_choice: C2 was added on 16 November 2026, after the lab named AIoT-VLA v10b for the follow task on 15 November 2026. It was added because that choice rests on a follow, and C1 is a GOTO to a coordinate that a follow-only model cannot fly. A test written after the choice it bears on is not a prediction: C2 describes the chosen backend, and compares it only with backends that flew the same test
C2_follow_closed_loop.scenario: the Project AirSim follow: 'follow a red car' in CityLife under the perception node's default signed bundle (follow_car_citylife), cruise altitude 8 m; the mission clock starts when the start gate passes (5 detector inferences in a row with a plausible box within 30 m)
C2_follow_closed_loop.rail: hil: Project AirSim and ArduPilot SITL on the desktop; MAVROS 2, the perception node (demo/pas_ardupilot/perception_node.py --pilot vla --mission follow), the Shield and the VLA server on the Jetson Orin
counts_as_c2: KPI-grade by the run's own kpi.json (hil, sim_speedup 1, signed bundle, clean commit)
no perception stressor, no policy hot-applied in flight, the scenario's own instruction (not a paraphrase)
flown alone: nothing else of the lab's running on the desktop or the Orin (no run folder records this; the flights known not to be are listed by hand in tools/vla_backend_table.py C2_NOT_ALONE)
the start gate passed (a flight that never started has no mission to score)
outputs: frac_within_30m: share of the mission's ticks with the aircraft within 30 m of the car's true position (metrics.json; the simulator's pose, evaluation only)
decision_hz_mission: answers the model parsed per second over the mission; decision_hz_asked: the same while it was being asked (not held by the rail, not withheld because the detector had no box)
C2_follow_closed_loop.reported: every flight on its own line and the range over the backend's C2 flights; a flight that lost the car is a C2 flight, not a discard
nulls: the hand-written follow on the same rail (--pilot servo): the no-learning reference
C2_follow_closed_loop.not_separated: the detector supplies the hint, and while it has no box the model is not asked: a C2 score is the model's and the detector's together

contradictions.claim: > mean efficiency 0.996, goal assist off" (section 6.4): those three
contradictions.note: states the assisted result as 'goal assist off'
contradictions.why: the fine-tune's 5/5 reached and 0.996 efficiency (training/eval_ft2_deploy.json) were flown with goal_blend 0.55, i.e. with the mission-direction assist ON. Its null does not separate it from the adapter before fine-tuning: under the same assist the original AerialVLA adapter also reached 5/5 (efficiency 0.942, training/eval_base_deploy.json), and the run3 fine-tune also reached 5/5 (training/eval_ft3_deploy.json). Without the assist (goal_blend 0) the run2 fine-tune reached 0/5 at yaw gain 1.0 (training/eval_ft2_e1.json) and 1/5 at yaw gain 0.4 (training/eval_ft2_yg04.json), and the original adapter 1/5 (training/eval_baseline.json). Correct statement: 5/5 reached (efficiency 0.996) with mission-direction assist (goal_blend 0.55); the original adapter under the same assist also reached 5/5 (0.942); without assist 0/5 (yaw gain 1.0) and 1/5 (yaw gain 0.4)

aerialvla_serving.choice: demo/vla_server_v2.py refuses to load the model until --precision, --attn and --merge/--no-merge are all given, and every response's identity carries the chosen configuration's agreement with the reference. Which configuration flies is decided by measuring CityLife's own VRAM beside the model (next wave): the bf16 rows fit only if the renderer and OWL-ViT leave about 17 GB of the 24 GB card free.
aerialvla_serving.choice_note: Why there is no default, and what each option costs (decided 2026-10-22, review of V1a). The precision changes what the model says: bf16 reproduces the upstream-precision reference - bf16/sdpa/unmerged gives the reference's output on 96 % of the 48 probe inputs, the merged bf16 rows on 88-90 % (greedy near-ties) - while every nf4 row agrees on only 25-33 % exactly and 48-50 % within 3 bins; 4-bit quantisation, not the attention kernel or the merge, is what moves the outputs. On the no-hint phrase every bf16 row and both nf4 merged rows answer '00 49 49 LAND' on 5 of 6 frames, while the nf4 unmerged loader (the one every earlier AerialVLA script here used) reproduces two of the 4 Aug malformed landing outputs ('00 49 4949', '00 49 494 49'); the strict reader turns those into holds. nf4/sdpa/merged is kept as the measured low-VRAM option (p50 517 ms; about 7.9 GB held by the process, 5.4 GB of it allocated by torch), not as a default that silently changes behaviour. A bf16 process holds about 16.8-16.9 GB: bf16/sdpa/unmerged (p50 486 ms) is the closest to the reference, bf16/sdpa/merged the fastest (p50 259 ms, below the paper's 0.35 s; its nvidia-smi reading failed, so its process VRAM is not recorded). The 10 GB budget behind the low-VRAM rule is an assumption, not a measurement: the card has 24 GB, desktop applications held about 3.4 GB before the runs (one reading, subtracted from every row's nvidia-smi figure), OWL-ViT takes 0.61 GB, and CityLife's own VRAM has never been logged. Measuring CityLife's VRAM beside the model is what decides which configuration flies (next wave); until then the server loads none by default.

g3.gate: If the chosen 7B-class VLA backend cannot produce 4-D actions at 10 Hz on the Orin in `int8` quantization, a gate could be added: "if Orin inference latency > 100 ms p95 by 2026-08-01, swap to a smaller / quantized backend (e.g. BitVLA, TinyVLA)." Whether to add this gate depends on Q2 measurement.
